chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ الْجَمِيلِ بْنِ دِرَاجٍ، عَنِ أَبَانِ بْنِ تَغْلِبَ، عَنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Diraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: لَوَدِدْتُ أَنْ أَصْحَابِي ضُرِبَتْ رُءُوسُهُمْ بِالسِّيَاطِ حَتَّى يَتَفَقَّهُوا

translations.en: I would have liked that my companions' heads were struck with whips until they gained comprehensive understanding (of the religion).

en.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) expresses a strong desire for his companions to acquire deep religious knowledge (fiqh), to the extent that he would accept even harsh physical discipline like being lashed with whips as a means to achieve this intellectual and spiritual goal. This highlights the paramount importance of understanding the religion in Shia tradition.
en.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by wanting his companions to be lashed with whips for knowledge?

key_terms.يَتَفَقَّهُوا: to gain comprehensive understanding of the religion
